transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m having a hard time keeping things organized. There are a lot of moving parts—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and lately I just can’t seem to sort them out in a useful way. I end up jumping to whatever feels most urgent or loudest instead of what actually matters, and it’s starting to catch up with me.
Have problems with organization and prioritizing been present since childhood?

Yes, looking back, it was there pretty early. In grade school, teachers would say I was bright, but I daydreamed a lot. I’d finish assignments and then forget to turn them in, or I’d lose my homework folders. That was happening well before I was a teenager.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or unusually irritable for several days in a row?

I don’t think so. I mean, I have stressful stretches where I’m more on edge, but I can’t think of a time where I was unusually energized or irritable for several days in a way that felt really out of character.
Do these problems with organization and follow-through affect you outside of work too?

Yes. It’s not just work. The same thing happens with anything that has a bunch of pieces to keep track of. I’ll have notes, deadlines, prep for things, decisions to make, and I just don’t sort them well. I end up doing whatever feels most urgent in the moment instead of what actually matters, and then I’m behind or things get missed.
Do you often get distracted when you’re trying to focus on a task or conversation?

Yes, pretty often. If I’m coding and Slack pings, or a tab flashes, or even just some visual idea pops into my head, I can completely lose the thread. Then I’ll realize I’ve spent twenty minutes going down some unrelated design rabbit hole instead of the thing I was supposed to be working on.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying?
I don’t think I spend a lot of time worrying, no. I get stressed about things I’m behind on, but it doesn’t feel like constant worrying all day.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to stay seated or still when you’re supposed to?

Yes, especially on long design calls. I’ll feel this pressure building in my body, like I need to get up and move. I’ll pace around my office or keep shifting from chair to chair, even though I’m trying to look like I’m sitting still and paying attention.
Do you often get so caught up trying to make something perfect that it delays you from finishing it?
I’m not really sure that’s a big issue for me. I can get stuck on details sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m usually trying to make things perfect to the point that it delays me finishing.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Not really, no. I get frustrated with myself when I’m behind or not getting things done, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed lately.
Do you often lose or misplace things you need, like keys, your phone, notes, or work materials?

Yes, pretty often. I’m constantly looking for things I need for work—USB-C adapters, my stylus, my sketchbook, even my badge. I’ll set something down and then have no memory of where I put it, and sometimes that can throw off a whole morning.
Over the past six months, have you been worrying excessively about a lot of different things on most days?
I don’t think so. I worry about things here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s excessive or happening most days across a lot of different things.
Have these attention and organization problems caused clear problems in your life, like missed deadlines, mistakes, or conflict with other people?

Yes. It’s starting to have real consequences at work. I missed a checkpoint for a patent filing, and there was a tough architecture review where I wasn’t as prepared or organized as I needed to be. After that, some collaborators were questioning whether I can actually lead the larger project, so… yeah, it’s affecting my reputation.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
I’m not sure I’d say hopeless. Frustrated, definitely, but I haven’t really noticed feeling like there’s no point or anything like that.
Do these attention and organization problems also cause difficulties at home or in other parts of your life outside work?

Mostly it’s been showing up at work, honestly. That’s where the real damage has been. I missed that patent filing checkpoint, and the architecture review went badly enough that people started questioning whether I can lead the bigger project. Outside of work, I’m not sure I’d point to anything as clearly as that.
